docs.title: Convert a Python Script to an Executable
Convert a Python Script to an Executable
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

A guide to packaging .py files into a standalone Windows .exe using Nuitka — with steps to eliminate antivirus false positives.

Note: PyInstaller is popular, but executables it produces are frequently flagged as malware by antivirus engines on VirusTotal. Nuitka compiles Python directly and, with the right configuration, produces clean binaries.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.9 (via Conda recommended)
  • Visual Studio Build Tools with the MSVC v14.2 component installed
  • Conda or pip for environment management
  • (Optional) osslsigncode for digital signing

docs.title: Set Up a Clean Virtual Environment
docs.text:
Nuitka compiles everything in your Python environment into the binary. A bloated environment means a bloated .exe. Start fresh.

conda create -n nuitka python=3.9
conda activate nuitka

Then install only the packages your script actually needs:

pip install <your-dependencies>

Note: Run your script in this minimal environment first to confirm it works before compiling.

docs.title: Install Nuitka
docs.text:
pip install nuitka

Note: If false positives become an issue after a Nuitka version becomes widely adopted, try pinning to a slightly older version: 

pip install nuitka==<older-version>

docs.title: Build the Executable
docs.text:
Run the following command from your project directory, replacing your_script.py with your script name:

python -m nuitka \
  --msvc=14.2 \
  --lto=no \
  --standalone \
  --onefile \
  --onefile-tempdir-spec=my_app_tempdir \
  --plugin-enable=pylint-warnings \
  --plugin-enable=tk-inter \
  --windows-disable-console \
  --windows-product-name="MyApp" \
  --windows-file-description="My Application" \
  --windows-product-version=1.0.0.0 \
  --windows-company-name="YourCompany" \
  --windows-icon-from-ico=C:\path\to\icon.ico \
  your_script.py

docs.title: Understand the Build Flags
docs.text:
Flag Purpose --msvc=14.2 Use the MSVC compiler. Less common than MinGW64, which reduces false positive rates. Alternatives: --clang, --mingw. --lto=no Disables Link Time Optimization. Speeds up the build. --standalone Bundles all dependencies into a dist/ folder. --onefile Compresses the dist/ folder into a single .exe. --onefile-tempdir-spec=<name> Sets where the .exe extracts itself at runtime. Without this, it extracts to %TEMP%. The folder is deleted automatically on exit. --plugin-enable=tk-inter Required if your script uses tkinter. --windows-disable-console Suppresses the console window at runtime. Note: print() statements will cause issues — comment them out before building. --windows-product-name Sets the product name in the executable's metadata. --windows-file-description Sets the file description in metadata. --windows-product-version Sets the version string (format: 0.0.0.0). --windows-company-name Sets the company name in metadata. --windows-icon-from-ico Assigns a custom icon to the executable.

Note: MSVC and Clang require installation via Visual Studio Installer → Modify → Individual Components. If you still get false positives, try recompiling with each of the four compilers (msvc, clang, mingw64, mingw) to find the cleanest result.

docs.title: Reduce False Positives
docs.text: Even a well-built Nuitka binary can trigger antivirus warnings. Check your result on VirusTotal and use the following strategies if needed.

docs.title: Strategy 1 — Fill in Executable Metadata
docs.text:
Antivirus engines treat anonymous binaries with more suspicion. Always set:

--windows-product-name
--windows-file-description
--windows-product-version
--windows-company-name

docs.title: Strategy 2 — Switch Compilers
docs.text:
Recompile using a different compiler. Each one produces a slightly different binary signature:

--msvc=14.2
--clang
--mingw64
--mingw

docs.title: Strategy 3 — Use an Older Nuitka Version
docs.text:
As a Nuitka version becomes more commonly used (including by malware authors), detection rates rise. Pinning to an older version can help:

pip install nuitka==1.x.x

docs.title: Sign the Executable
docs.text: Digital signing is the most effective solution. In testing, signing reduced a VirusTotal result from 13 detections to 0.

docs.title: Tools Needed
docs.text:
• A certificate (.crt / .key), either self-signed or from a CA
  • osslsigncode — an open-source cross-platform signing tool

docs.title: Sign the Executable
docs.text:
osslsigncode sign \
  -certs your_cert.crt \
  -key your_key.key \
  -in your_app.exe \
  -out your_app_signed.exe

Note: You can also use signtool.exe (from the Windows SDK) with a .pfx certificate as an alternative.

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text: Issue Detail Japanese (multibyte) folder names Signed onefile .exe files fail to extract if there are Japanese or other multibyte characters in the folder path. Unsigned executables are unaffected. Workaround for path issue Use the unsigned dist/ folder directly instead of the onefile .exe, or ensure the extraction path contains only ASCII characters. print() with --windows-disable-console Console output has no target, which can cause crashes. Comment out all print() calls before building. Persistent false positives Occasionally one detection may remain even after signing. No known complete fix; rotating compilers and Nuitka versions is the best mitigation.

docs.title: Create an Executable from a Python Script
Create an Executable from a Python Script
docs.text: Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

docs.title: Recommended Tool: Nuitka
docs.text:
Nuitka compiles Python source code into a native C-based executable. The resulting binary runs without requiring Python to be installed on the target machine.

Note: PyInstaller is a popular alternative, but executables it produces are frequently flagged as malware by antivirus engines. Nuitka compiles Python directly and produces cleaner binaries.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python installed
  • A C compiler (on Windows, Nuitka will prompt to install the MinGW-w64 compiler automatically if none is found)

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Install Nuitka.

    pip install nuitka

  2. Compile the script into a standalone executable.

    python -m nuitka --standalone --onefile your_script.py
    Option Description --standalone Includes all dependencies so the executable runs on machines without Python --onefile Packages everything into a single .exe file

  3. Find the output executable in the current directory (e.g., your_script.exe on Windows).

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The first build takes longer than PyInstaller because Nuitka compiles Python to C and then compiles the C code.
  • For GUI apps, add --disable-console to suppress the terminal window.
  • To package the resulting executable into a Windows installer, see Create an Installer for a Python App.

docs.text:

A free Windows installer builder. Use it after PyInstaller to wrap the executable into a proper Windows installer (.exe) with install/uninstall support, shortcuts, and a setup wizard.

  2. Download and install Inno Setup.

  4. Compile the script to produce the final installer .exe.

pip install cx_Freeze

docs.title: Check Pinokio Support for Style-Bert-VITS2
docs.text:

No official Pinokio script for Style-Bert-VITS2 exists. This page summarizes the current state of Pinokio support and the alternatives available.

docs.title: Current State
docs.text:

  • No community-made pinokio.js / install.json scripts for it have been published publicly.

docs.title: Why It Works Fine Without Pinokio
docs.text: Style-Bert-VITS2 already supports a one-click-style installation through bundled .bat scripts. Download the ZIP, extract it, and double-click Install-Style-Bert-VITS2.bat (GPU) or the CPU variant. No Git or Python knowledge is required, which is close to Pinokio's own one-click philosophy. See Set Up Style-Bert-VITS2 WebUI for the full setup process.

docs.title: Options if You Still Want Pinokio
docs.text:
• Use the .bat installer directly: This is the officially recommended path, and arguably simpler than Pinokio for this tool.
  • Write your own Pinokio script: Any GitHub repository with a pinokio.js plus install.js / start.js scripts can be installed through Pinokio. You can write these scripts to clone the Style-Bert-VITS2 repository and run the equivalent of the .bat steps with shell.run.
  • Use it as a Python library: For synthesis-only use, Style-Bert-VITS2 is published as a pip package (pip install style-bert-vits2) and runs on CPU without an NVIDIA GPU. This suits integration scenarios, such as connecting to YMM4 through its API, more than a standalone WebUI setup.

docs.title: Set Up Style-Bert-VITS2 WebUI
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Style-Bert-VITS2 is a free, open-source text-to-speech engine that supports Japanese, English, and Chinese. It runs locally on your PC and can be connected to YMM4 as a voice engine.

docs.title: What is Style-Bert-VITS2?
docs.text:
• Developed by litagin02, based on the original Bert-VITS2 project
  • Not YMM4-specific — it is a general-purpose TTS engine
  • Connects to YMM4 via a local API server (similar to VOICEVOX and CoeiroInk)
  • Supports multiple languages including English with the right voice model
Bert-VITS2 (original)
    └── Style-Bert-VITS2 (litagin02's fork, adds style control)
            └── AivisSpeech (uses Style-Bert-VITS2 as its engine)

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Windows 10/11
  • Python 3.12.x
  • ~5 GB free disk space (for models and dependencies)
  • NVIDIA GPU recommended but not required (CPU works for inference)

docs.title: Step 1: Download Style-Bert-VITS2
docs.text:
1. Go to the Style-Bert-VITS2 GitHub repository.
  2. Click the green Code button → Download ZIP.
  3. Extract to a folder with no Japanese characters or spaces in the path.

Warning: The path must not contain Japanese characters or spaces. Example of a valid path: D:\00-portable-apps\Style-Bert-VITS2-master

docs.title: Step 2: Set Up the Virtual Environment
docs.text:
Open a terminal in the extracted folder and run the following commands one by one.

Create the venv:

python -m venv venv

Activate the venv:

venv\Scripts\activate

You should see (venv) at the start of your prompt.

Verify Python version:

python --version

Python 3.12.x is recommended.

docs.title: Step 3: Install Dependencies
docs.text:
This version of Style-Bert-VITS2 includes requirements-infer.txt for inference-only use (lighter than the full requirements.txt, which includes training tools).

Install inference dependencies:

pip install -r requirements-infer.txt

Note: This will take several minutes as it downloads PyTorch and other large packages.

Upgrade PyTorch to the latest version (required — the version pinned in requirements-infer.txt is too old):

pip install torch torchaudio --upgrade

Upgrade pip (optional but recommended):

python.exe -m pip install --upgrade pip

docs.title: Step 4: Initialize (Download Models)
docs.text:
Run initialize.py with the --only_infer flag to skip downloading heavy training models:

python initialize.py --only_infer

This downloads:

  • BERT language models (including English deberta-v3-large)
  • Default Japanese voice models (jvnv-F1-jp, jvnv-F2-jp, jvnv-M1-jp, jvnv-M2-jp, koharune-ami, amitaro)

Note: The script may complete silently with no output — this is normal. Verify by checking that the bert\ and model_assets\ folders were created and populated.

docs.title: Step 5: Launch the WebUI
docs.text:
python app.py

The WebUI will open automatically in your browser at http://127.0.0.1:7860.

Note: To launch in future sessions, activate the venv first, then run python app.py: 

venv\Scripts\activate
python app.py

docs.title: WebUI Overview
docs.text: Element Japanese Romaji Description Model list モデル一覧 Moderu ichiran Select a voice model Load button ロード Rōdo Load the selected model Text input テキスト Tekisuto Enter text to synthesize Language Language — Select JP / EN / ZH Synthesize button 音声合成 Onsei gōsei Generate the voice Style スタイル Sutairu Emotional style of the voice

docs.title: Default Voice Models
docs.text:
Model Type jvnv-F1-jp Japanese female 1 jvnv-F2-jp Japanese female 2 jvnv-M1-jp Japanese male 1 jvnv-M2-jp Japanese male 2 koharune-ami Japanese female (Koharune Ami) amitaro Japanese female (Amitaro)

Note: The default models are Japanese only. To use native English TTS, an English-trained model such as the RikkaBotan model must be added separately.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Keep the terminal window open while using the WebUI — closing it stops the server.
  • The venv must be activated each session before launching.
  • The PyTorch upgrade (pip install torch torchaudio --upgrade) is required due to a version conflict with the transformers library.

docs.text:
When you drag multiple images into a Markdown file in VS Code, they are inserted on a single line like this:

![Photo](img/00-images/room01-01.jpg) ![Photo](img/00-images/room01-02.jpg) ![Photo](img/00-images/room01-03.jpg)

But often you want each image on its own line:

![Photo](img/00-images/room01-01.jpg)
![Photo](img/00-images/room01-02.jpg)
![Photo](img/00-images/room01-03.jpg)

You can fix this instantly using Find and eeplace with regular expressions.

Replace:

\n![

Click:

Replace All

docs.text:
Pattern Meaning \s matches a space ![ matches the Markdown image start \n inserts a newline

So this converts:

(space)![

into

(newline)![

This version only affects Markdown images:

Find:

\)\s+!\[

Replace:

)\n![

This ensures replacement only happens between images.

After:

docs.title: Fix Python Interpreter Path Not Found in VS Code
Fix Python Interpreter Path Not Found in VS Code
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

When VS Code shows a warning about python.defaultInterpreterPath pointing to a path that no longer exists, the Python interpreter VS Code was previously configured to use has been deleted or moved.

Common causes:

  • You deleted a virtual environment folder.
  • You uninstalled or moved a Python installation.
  • The project was opened on a different machine with a different folder structure.

docs.title: Fix: Select a New Interpreter
docs.text:
1. Open the Command Palette:

    • Windows/Linux: Ctrl+Shift+P
    • Mac: Cmd+Shift+P

    If the shortcut doesn't work, go to Help → Show All Commands in the menu bar.

  2. Type Python: Select Interpreter and press Enter.

  3. Select the interpreter you want to use from the dropdown. VS Code marks the recommended one with a Recommended label.

Label What It Means Recommended System Python installed from python.org Conda Python from an Anaconda/Miniconda environment (path shown) A specific virtual environment

VS Code updates the setting automatically and the warning disappears.

docs.title: Understanding the Setting
docs.text:
python.defaultInterpreterPath stores the file path to a python.exe (Windows) or python (Mac/Linux) executable. VS Code uses this interpreter for:

  • Running scripts
  • IntelliSense and code completion
  • Linting and formatting
  • The integrated terminal

docs.title: Default Installation Paths
docs.text: Source Typical Path python.org (Windows) ~\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python3xx\python.exe python.org (Mac) /usr/local/bin/python3 Miniconda/Anaconda C:\ProgramData\miniconda3\python.exe Virtual environment <project_folder>\venv\Scripts\python.exe (Windows)

docs.title: Edit the Setting Manually (Alternative)
docs.text: If the Command Palette approach does not work, edit the setting directly.

docs.title: Method 1: Edit in Settings UI
docs.text:
1. Go to File → Preferences → Settings (or Ctrl+,).
  2. Search for python.defaultInterpreterPath.
  3. Clear the existing invalid path and enter the correct one, or leave it blank to let VS Code auto-detect.

docs.text:
1. Open the Command Palette → Open User Settings (JSON).
  2. Find the line: 
    "python.defaultInterpreterPath": "D:\\old\\path\\to\\python.exe"
  3. Update or delete it.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• If you are using a virtual environment, activate or recreate it before selecting it as the interpreter.
  • python.defaultInterpreterPath is a fallback — once you select an interpreter for a workspace, VS Code stores it separately and uses that instead.
  • To check which interpreter is currently active, look at the status bar at the bottom-left of the VS Code window.

docs.title: The home and homes Folders
docs.text:
In Synology NAS, home and homes are two views of the same data — no files are duplicated.

  • homes folder: The parent folder for all user home directories on the NAS (visible to admins only by default).
  • home folder: A shortcut to the currently logged-in user's personal folder.

When you back up to Personal Space, photos are saved to:

  • Actual path: /homes/<username>/Photos/MobileBackup/...
  • Your shortcut: /home/Photos/MobileBackup/...

Both paths point to the same files.

docs.title: Recommended Settings for a Single-User NAS
docs.text:
If you are running the NAS as a private personal environment:

  1. Enable User Home — this is required.
  2. Set the backup destination in Synology Photos to Personal Space.
  3. Check permissions — if other users are registered on the NAS, confirm they cannot access the homes folder (the default setting) to keep your photos private.

docs.title: Storage Usage
docs.text: If storage usage appears to spike in Storage Manager, this is not caused by duplicate data. It reflects background processing such as index creation, thumbnail generation, and metadata management — all of which run quickly on a DS720+ with WD Red SA500 SSDs.

docs.title: Understand Why Mobile Backup Creates Year and Month Folders
Understand Why Mobile Backup Creates Year and Month Folders
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Note: This procedure is based on Pixel 8a (Android).

docs.title: The Folder Structure Is Built In
docs.text:
Synology Photos always organizes mobile backups by device, year, and month. Files land at:

/home/Photos/MobileBackup/<device-name>/<year>/<month>/

This applies to every backup source you select — Camera, Screenshots, or any custom folder. There is no setting in Synology Photos to disable the year/month subfolders or back up into a flat folder instead.

docs.title: Workarounds
docs.text:
If the subfolders bother you, consider one of these approaches instead of fighting the built-in structure:

  • Browse with Timeline view. Synology Photos shows all backed-up images in chronological order regardless of their folder location, so you never need to look at the year/month subfolders during normal use.
  • Use a third-party sync app. Apps such as FolderSync (Android) can sync a folder on your phone directly to a NAS share over SMB or WebDAV, giving you full control over the destination path — including a flat one.
  • Run a periodic flattening script. Set up a script in DSM Task Scheduler that moves files out of the year/month subfolders into the parent folder and removes the empty subfolders afterward.

Note: Option one requires no extra setup and works well for most people. Options two and three replace or supplement the built-in backup and need more configuration.

docs.title: Charge the Tablet
docs.text:
There are three ways to charge the tablet:

  1. Official charger (preferred): Use the standard charger plug and data cable included with the tablet.
  2. Third-party charger: Use a charger plug and data cable from another tablet or phone brand. Preferred specifications: 9V2A or 5V3A.

  3. PC charging via USB:

    1. Connect the tablet to the PC with a Type-C cable (a USB adapter may be required).
    2. On the tablet, select Charge the device from the pop-up window.

Note: Charge the tablet with the screen off when possible — charging while the screen is on extends the charging time. Use the official charger when available.

docs.title: Charge Another Phone in Reverse
docs.text:
The tablet has an 8000 mAh battery when fully charged. You can use it to temporarily charge an Android phone.

  1. Connect the tablet to the Android phone using a USB-C to USB-C cable.
  2. On the tablet, select Use as power supply from the pop-up window.

Note: Reverse charging supports Android phones only — not iOS devices. The output is approximately 2W, which is suitable for emergency use but not for everyday charging.

docs.text:

Several apps let you use the Magic Drawing Pad as a wireless pen display on Windows 11. They fall into two categories: display extension apps and remote desktop apps. For Blender, only display extension apps are practical.

docs.title: Display Extension Apps
docs.text:
These apps add the tablet as an extra Windows monitor. The stylus works as pen input on that display.

App Price Strength Limitation SpaceDesk Free Broad device support Pen experience varies; may need tweaking SuperDisplay Paid Polished pen experience for artists Focused on drawing; less general-purpose Duet Display Paid Reliable, low latency Subscription-based Weylus Free & open source Full stylus and pressure sensitivity via browser; no account required Requires vJoy driver setup; browser-based interface

docs.title: Remote Desktop Apps
docs.text:
These apps stream the entire Windows desktop to the tablet as a video feed. The tablet does not appear as a second monitor in Windows — it shows a mirrored or remote view of the existing display.

App Why It Does Not Work for This Use Case Chrome Remote Desktop Streams the desktop as video; stylus input is treated as mouse clicks with no pressure sensitivity Microsoft Remote Desktop Same limitation; designed for remote access, not display extension

Blender relies on pressure-sensitive stylus input for sculpting and texture painting. Remote desktop apps do not pass stylus pressure data through, making them unsuitable for this workflow.

docs.title: Set Up Weylus
docs.text:
1. Download Weylus for Windows from GitHub.
  2. Install a virtual stylus driver: the setup wizard guides you through installing vJoy or the Weylus driver to enable pressure sensitivity in Windows.
  3. Run Weylus on your PC. It displays a local URL such as 192.168.x.x:8001 and a QR code.
  4. Open a web browser on your tablet, enter the URL, and your PC screen appears.
  5. In the Weylus browser interface on your tablet, check Capture Stylus and Pressure Sensitivity.

docs.title: Why SpaceDesk
docs.text:
SpaceDesk works well when:

  • You already have a large Android drawing tablet and want to use it without extra cost.
  • Your PC and tablet are on the same local network.
  • You need an extra monitor with pen input for Blender rather than a dedicated drawing workspace.
  • The use case does not require a professional or portable studio setup.

For Blender work in particular, having the tablet as an additional display with stylus input is enough for most workflows. SpaceDesk provides this at no cost.
